output.title: When bookkeeping habits stop helping
output.body:
If your bookkeeping habit only records what already happened, it is not yet a workflow control. It is a ledger, not a decision rule.

That matters for a small-business owner because the real question is simple: does this recurring step help you decide what to pay, what to chase, or what to review next week? If it does, keep it. If it does not, it is probably just tidy admin.

A useful test is to pick one repeating bookkeeping task and write down three things: the input, the rule, and the output. For example, an invoice arrives in email, a category is chosen, and the line ends up in the sheet. If you cannot write those three parts plainly, the habit is probably too loose to automate or delegate cleanly.

That does not mean every bookkeeping habit needs changing. It means you should separate routine recordkeeping from a repeatable decision. For a founder, that is usually the part worth looking at first.

As a rule of thumb, if the task is digital, repeats the same way, and ends in a yes/no or categorization decision, it may be worth a closer look. Scan-heavy PDF work is a different case and is not the one to start with.
